items.text: Harbourview Chest Imaging. LDCT lung screening, annual round. Findings: 4 mm solid nodule right upper lobe, stable in appearance. Comparison: the 2025 exam was reported as Lung-RADS 3 because of a since-resolved ground-glass focus. Impression: Lung-RADS 2 for the current exam. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

LOW DOSE CT CHEST - SCREENING. 8 mm part-solid nodule left lower lobe, new since baseline. OVERALL: Lung-RADS 4A. Note: should the solid component enlarge on the 3-month study, the category would become 4B. No lymphadenopathy. Recommend 3-month LDCT or PET-CT per local pathway.

Screening LDCT, Al Noor Medical Tower. History: last year's exam was called 4A for a 9 mm nodule in the lingula; that opacity has completely resolved on today's scan. No new nodules. Mild centrilobular emphysema. Final category for this exam: 1. Return to annual screening.

Referral form (pre-filled by primary care): suspected Lung-RADS 3, 6-month follow-up. Radiologist report: 3 mm calcified granuloma right middle lobe, no other pulmonary nodules, no suspicious findings. The referral category is not supported; final Lung-RADS category 2. Next screen 12 months.

LDCT screening report. Prior (Nov 2025): Lung-RADS 2. Current: new 7 mm solid nodule right lower lobe, smooth margins, no prior at this site. Lung-RADS 3 for this exam. For reference only, a solid nodule of 15 mm or more here would be categorised 4B. Six-month LDCT advised.

Findings by nodule. Nodule 1, RUL, 3 mm solid: category 2. Nodule 2, LUL, 5 mm solid: category 2. Nodule 3, RLL, 8 mm solid, new: category 3. Background mild bronchial wall thickening. No overall category line is recorded in this section; see clinic for next steps.

Cedar Grove Radiology - LDCT. Multiple findings. (a) 6 mm solid nodule RUL, growing slowly compared with 2025: 4A. (b) 4 mm perifissural nodule LLL: 2. (c) 11 mm solid nodule RML with spiculation and a new ipsilateral hilar node: 4X. No final category entered in the template.

LDCT SCREEN. Lung-RADS category 2 (overall). Supporting detail: nodule A 3 mm RUL (2), nodule B 5 mm LLL, solid, unchanged (2), nodule C 2 mm subpleural calcified (1). Coronary calcification noted. Annual screening in 12 months.

Annual LDCT. Two findings. 1) 9 mm solid nodule LUL, new: assessed 4A. 2) 14 mm irregular solid nodule RLL with pleural thickening and mediastinal adenopathy: 4B on nodule features. Overall assessment: Lung-RADS 4X given the additional adverse features. Discuss at MDT.

Per-lesion table: L1 right apex 2 mm - category 1/2 region, not counted; L2 left lingula 6 mm part-solid, solid component 3 mm - category 3; L3 right base 4 mm solid, unchanged - category 2. The reporting system did not generate an exam-level category. Radiologist initials pending.

Hospital of the Gulf Coast, Thoracic Radiology. Technique: low-dose, 1.0 mm recon. Findings: lungs clear. No nodules, no consolidation. Mild emphysema. Impression: negative screening examination. Continue annual LDCT.
LDCT screening examination. A 6 mm ground-glass nodule in the left upper lobe is present. In the reader's view it is probably benign. Short-interval CT in six months recommended to confirm.

IMPRESSION: A 13 mm solid nodule with lobulated margins in the right upper lobe, growing from the prior study. This is a suspicious nodule. No adenopathy, no effusion. Recommend diagnostic CT chest and pulmonology review.

Screening LDCT summary: 22 mm spiculated mass left upper lobe, very suspicious for primary bronchogenic carcinoma, with enlarged ipsilateral hilar and subcarinal nodes and a small malignant-appearing pleural effusion. Urgent multidisciplinary referral requested.
Findings: 5 mm densely calcified nodule right lower lobe, typical of a healed granuloma. Benign appearance. No change vs prior. Continue annual screening per programme.

LDCT screening. Examination degraded by severe respiratory motion artefact through the lower zones; nodules cannot be reliably assessed. Category 0 - incomplete. Repeat low-dose scan recommended within the next few weeks.

Report body: 7 mm solid nodule RLL. Summary line: Final category Lung-RADS 2. Recommendations box (auto-filled from template): Final category Lung-RADS 4A, refer for diagnostic work-up. Unsigned draft.
LDCT lung screening - technical details only. Scanner: 64-slice. kVp 100, CTDIvol 1.4 mGy. Patient positioned supine, breath-hold adequate. [Report continues on next page - page not available.]

LDCT screen. A 10 mm area of airspace opacity in the left lower lobe is likely to reflect an infective or inflammatory process. Cannot be classified until comparison with outside imaging; prior CT has been requested from the referring hospital and is awaited. Category 0. Re-review once received.
Chest LDCT. There is a 6 mm nodule in the right middle lobe. Emphysema, moderate. Aortic valve calcification. Clinical correlation is advised. No further comment.

ADDENDUM to LDCT of 28 Oct. After retrieval of the 2025 study, the 5 mm RUL nodule is unchanged for over a year. The original category of 3 is revised. Revised overall category: 2S (S for moderate coronary artery calcification). Annual screening.

Addendum - second read. The original report of this exam called the left upper lobe nodule Lung-RADS 4A. Following consensus review with a second thoracic radiologist, the final overall category for this exam is amended to Lung-RADS 3; the nodule is considered probably benign. 6-month LDCT.

Referral form box: Lung-RADS 4B - urgent respiratory clinic. Radiology report: the referral categorisation is not accepted. Only a 2 mm calcified nodule and emphysema are seen. Lung-RADS 2S. No urgent referral is required.

ADDENDUM: Incidental finding of marked coronary artery calcification is added to the report (S modifier applies). This does not alter the lung assessment. The category for the 12 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe remains 4A, as originally issued.

Addendum, clinical information received: patient had a febrile chest illness two weeks before the scan. The multifocal consolidation is likely infective. Referral had stated category 2; this is overridden. Category 0 - repeat LDCT in 1 to 3 months after treatment.

Respiratory MDT clinic note, 4 Nov. The patient was invited for review of the Lung-RADS 4A nodule and did not attend. Two phone calls unanswered. Letter sent with new appointment. No work-up performed.
PET-CT booking outcome: patient DNA'd the PET-CT scan on 30 Oct after the screening CT showed a 14 mm spiculated nodule. Slot has been released. Will be re-offered through the nurse navigator.
Interventional radiology list. CT-guided lung biopsy planned for 6 Nov for LDCT 4B lesion. Failed to attend; family says patient was travelling. No tissue obtained. Referring doctor informed.

Outpatient pulmonology. Previously (2024) an unrelated biopsy of a cervical lymph node was benign. For the present screening finding, the patient was a no-show at today's 09:30 appointment. Nothing further discussed.

Case had been listed for MDT discussion on 2 Nov together with the clinic visit. The patient did not attend the clinic; the team reviewed images alone and recommend rebooking the patient for assessment before any plan is made.

Seen in clinic with husband. Having discussed risks of CT-guided biopsy for the 4A lesion, the patient declined the procedure at this time and wishes to think it over. No tissue. Will phone clinic if she changes her mind.
Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy of the LUL nodule completed on 3 Nov without complication. Histopathology awaited; expected in 5 working days. Results to be reviewed in clinic then.
Attended for planned bronchoscopy but had a productive cough, fever 38.2, and the procedure was postponed by the anaesthetist. Antibiotics given. New date to be arranged once recovered.

Cytology from EBUS needle aspirate: preliminary report shows atypical cells suspicious for malignancy; final cell-block and immunostains outstanding. Case to be added to next week's MDT list. No treatment referral made yet.

Clinic review of the 4B nodule. PET-CT is booked for 12 Nov. The case has not yet been discussed at MDT; this is planned after the PET result. No tissue sampling yet. Patient understands the sequence.

Pathology: adenocarcinoma, acinar pattern, RUL. Lung cancer MDT on 29 Oct reviewed imaging and histology and recommended lobectomy. Referred to thoracic surgery; pre-operative assessment booked. Patient informed.

Biopsy result: non-small cell carcinoma. Referred to medical oncology for systemic therapy discussion. Patient anxious. Follow up with oncology next week. The note does not record any multidisciplinary meeting.
Histology: squamous cell carcinoma, left lower lobe, stage I. Patient unfit for surgery (severe COPD). MDT decision 3 Nov: stereotactic body radiotherapy. Referral to radiation oncology sent today.

PET avid 20 mm RUL mass; biopsy was non-diagnostic and no tissue is available. MDT reviewed the case and recommended surgical resection. Referral to thoracic surgery sent. No pathological diagnosis exists at present.
Small cell lung carcinoma confirmed on core biopsy. Discussed at lung MDT on 5 Nov; consensus for chemo-radiotherapy. Referred to oncology and radiotherapy, first visit booked for 9 Nov.
Result of CT-guided biopsy of the 4A nodule: necrotising granuloma, no malignancy, stains negative for organisms. Reassured. Plan: return to annual LDCT screening in 12 months.
The consolidation seen on screening has resolved fully on follow-up diagnostic CT. No biopsy was needed. MDT decision recorded 7 Nov: return to the annual screening programme.
Chest clinic follow-up of Lung-RADS 4A report. Patient well. Return to annual screening. See you next year.
Biopsy of 12 mm RLL nodule: pulmonary hamartoma, non-malignant. Counselled. Will be returned to the annual lung screening pathway; letter to GP.

Review after antibiotics and repeat imaging. The opacity is consistent with benign inflammatory change. The MDT agreed annual screening is appropriate and it was discussed with the patient. Next LDCT in 12 months.
Transthoracic biopsy: fibrous tissue and chronic inflammation, benign. Nodule remains indeterminate in size, 7 mm. Plan: repeat CT chest in 3 months and review with results.
Diagnostic CT shows a stable 8 mm ground-glass nodule. Biopsy not indicated at this stage. We will do an interval CT in 6 months and the patient will see us again after it.
Screening LDCT report. Technique low dose. 9 mm solid nodule right upper lobe, new. Lung-RADS 4A. Recommend diagnostic evaluation. Signed by reporting radiologist.
Pathology confirms adenocarcinoma in the right lower lobe nodule. After consultation the plan is to return to the annual screening programme and repeat LDCT in 12 months. Letter sent.

Review of the 5 mm to 9 mm nodule: needle biopsy reported atypical cells, no evidence of malignancy. Case discussed at MDT, which advised interval CT in 3 months. Patient booked for imaging; clinic review after that.
Nurse clinic follow-up. Patient did not attend today's appointment despite two reminder texts. Screening BP was 152/96 and HbA1c 6.8% on the original panel. Will mail a new appointment.
DNA - second review slot for raised LDL. Attempted call at 11:00, no answer. Voicemail left. Reschedule via call centre.
Follow-up visit for abnormal screening (BMI 33, BP 148/92, fasting glucose elevated). Patient failed to attend. No assessment possible. Closed pending rebooking.
Family medicine recall. No-show. Employer reports patient was on night shift. Old note: statin discussed last year. Offer evening slot.
Did not attend scheduled post-screening consultation of 5 Nov. Quoted results from last year: HbA1c 6.8%, BP 150/94. Patient not seen, no examination or plan.
Seen for raised BP at screening. Repeat clinic readings 156/98 and 154/96 confirm hypertension. Amlodipine 5 mg started today, home BP diary given, review in 4 weeks.

Repeat HbA1c 7.4% confirms type 2 diabetes. Metformin started and dietitian appointment booked for 14 Nov. Repeat lipid panel: LDL 212 mg/dL confirmed, atorvastatin 40 mg prescribed. BP and weight not discussed at this visit.
BMI re-measured at 34.2 kg/m2, class I obesity confirmed. Enrolled in the clinic's 12-week weight management programme today; first group session on Sunday.

Comprehensive review. Hypertension confirmed on repeat (158/100): ramipril 5 mg started. HbA1c repeat 7.1%: diabetes, referred to the diabetes clinic, referral sent. BMI 32: enrolled in lifestyle programme. Lipids were normal and were not reviewed further.
Confirmatory fasting lipids: LDL 4.9 mmol/L, raised, rosuvastatin commenced. BMI 31.5 confirmed; referred to dietitian, appointment made. Counselled on diet and exercise.
Screening BP 164/102. Today's clinic reading 160/100. Not yet labelled hypertensive: asked to take two weeks of home readings and 24-hour ambulatory monitoring booked. Decision after results.
Random glucose 240 mg/dL at screening; repeat fasting glucose ordered, sample taken this morning. LDL 205: statin offered but patient declined for now and wants to read about it. Will revisit.
HbA1c repeated at 8.2%, so diabetes is confirmed. We ran out of time; treatment plan to be agreed at the next visit. Nothing started.
BMI 36. Offered weight programme but patient deferred until after Ramadan-travel plans. BP 146/94 at screening - repeat result is awaited from the lab after a nurse measurement; no decision yet.
Repeat lipid profile awaited, blood drawn today. Glucose was noted to be elevated at screening. Patient advised about results call. Nothing else recorded.
Repeat BP in clinic 126/78 and home average 122/76; the screening value of 150/95 was probably white-coat effect. No treatment required. Routine rescreen in 1 year.
HbA1c 6.0%: prediabetes range. Given advice on diet and walking, leaflet provided. No medicine and no referral at this stage. Rescreen in a year.

Confirmatory tests today. Repeat HbA1c 5.4%, normal - original sample was probably mislabelled. LDL repeat 118 mg/dL, below threshold; the first value 196 was a lab error. Both back to routine screening.
Prediabetes (HbA1c 6.2%): dietary advice given, routine re-screening in 12 months. Repeat blood pressure 130/82 - normal, returns to routine screening. Patient reassured.
Screening BMI of 31 was a data entry error: height recorded as 1.45 m rather than 1.65 m. Re-measured BMI 27.8. No weight programme needed.
Attended for a review. Last year LDL was 195 and BP 150/92 but this visit patient only wanted a medication refill for allergy symptoms and a sick-note. No screening result was discussed.
Header: known hypertension, type 2 diabetes. Presenting complaint today: lower back pain after lifting. Examined, analgesia given, physiotherapy advised. Screening abnormalities were not mentioned.
DISCHARGE SUMMARY. Admitted with community-acquired pneumonia, treated with IV antibiotics for 5 days, discharged on oral amoxicillin. Chest X-ray improving. Follow up with GP in 2 weeks.
BP confirmed hypertensive on repeat, 154/96; amlodipine started today. Plan section (from template): BP normal on repeat, return to routine screening, no treatment needed.

Patient attended with spouse. Spouse has diabetes and is on insulin. Patient has no history of diabetes and no family clinic action was taken for the patient. Discussion was about the spouse's glucose sensor only.
